hints.title: Complementary Windowing
hints.text: Sharing k contiguous candies is equivalent to removing a sliding window of length k from your flavor count.

hints.title: Global Frequency Initialization
hints.text: Start with the frequency count of all candies, then remove the first k elements to represent the initial gift.

hints.title: Rolling Window Adjustment
hints.text: Slide the window rightwards by restoring the element leaving on the left and removing the new element entering on the right.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def shareCandies(self, candies: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        freq = Counter(candies)
        n = len(candies)

        for i in range(k):
            freq[candies[i]] -= 1
            if freq[candies[i]] == 0:
                del freq[candies[i]]

        max_unique = len(freq)

        for i in range(k, n):
            # Outgoing from window (restored to user)
            left_candy = candies[i - k]
            freq[left_candy] += 1

            # Incoming to window (given away)
            right_candy = candies[i]
            freq[right_candy] -= 1
            if freq[right_candy] == 0:
                del freq[right_candy]

            max_unique = max(max_unique, len(freq))

        return max_unique
```

complexity.space: O(U) frequency table of distinct flavors
variables: k: contiguous window size to share
complexity.notes: Sliding window of size k represents shared candies; maximize remaining flavors with positive count.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Re-counting unique flavors for each candidate window takes O(N * (N - k)) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining frequency map updates in O(1) per step enables linear time execution.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should maintain outside window flavor frequencies with a sliding window.
